70 American Builder, July 1935.

Selected List of Manufacturers’ Literature

For the Service of Builders, Contractors, Architects and Dealers

THE publications listed on these pages may be obtained without charge either by using the coupon, listing the numbers of the catalogs desired and mailing to American Builder, 105 West Adams Street, Chicago, or by applying on your business stationery to the manufacturers direct, in which case kindly mention this publication. Either the titles or the numbers may be used in ordering. This list is an editorial feature for convenience of our readers.

MASONRY MATERIALS

Portland Cement Assn., 33 W. Grand Ave., Chicago, Ill.

428—Earthquake-Proof Construction—“Analysis of Small Monolithic Concrete Buildings for Earthquake Forces,” a handbook of 56 pages analyzing various details of construction and their resistance to earthquake shock. A pioneer work on this subject for the small construction industry.

Louisville Cement Co., Louisville, Ky.

430—Mortar—“Brixment for Perfect Mortar,” a 4-page specification and discussion of Brixment and its use for masonry mortar, including colored mortar.

National Lime Assn., Washington, D.C.

431—Mortar—“Lime Mortar, Its Relation to Water-Tight Masonry,” a 36-page handbook discussing various mortar formulae, their characteristics and reaction to tests.

CARPENTRY MATERIALS

The Upson Co., Lockport, N.Y.

432—De Luxe Wallboard Finish—“Classic Ceilings,” a beautifully illustrated brochure showing how to secure paneled walls and ceilings of truly artistic worth. A complete handbook of modern wallboard practice.

The Insulite Co., Minneapolis, Minn.

434—Warm Garage Plans—“How to Solve Your Garage Problem”; plans for one- and two-car garages of Insulite Board are presented in quarter-inch scale drawings with wall detail 1½ inches to the foot.

Huttig Mfg. Co., Muscatine, Iowa.

435—Window Frames—“Clear Pine Frames with Aluminum Primed Joints,” a 6-page illustrated folder giving full details of this improved window frame.

HARDWARE SPECIALTIES

Micklin Mfg. Co., Omaha, Nebr.

436—Frame Corners—“Features of Micklin Dual and Single Corners,” a leaflet illustrating several uses for this ingenious little reinforcing corner—helps to build strong screens, tables, shelves, doors, etc.

Allmetal Weatherstrip Co., 231 W. Illinois St., Chicago, Ill.

437—Weatherstrip Opportunities—A weatherstrippers’ sales kit is offered to ambitious carpenters and builders who want to push weatherstrip selling and installing as a business.

Timber Engineering Co., 1337 Connecticut Ave., N.W., Washington, D.C.

438—Barn Frame Connectors—“Trusses for Farm Structures”; construction drawing sheet analyzing several types of plank frame barn roof trusses made stronger and simpler by the use of Teco steel connections.

Allith-Prouty Co., Danville, Ill.

439—Heavy Door Hangers—“Allith Airport Door Harware,” an illustrated catalog of 100 pages showing best examples of commercial airports and how the big doors are hung and operated.

The F. E. Myers & Bro. Co., Ashland, Ohio.

440—Builders’ Hardware—“Myers Door Hanger Catalog,” the 1935 edition, is a catalog of 24 pages presenting full details of the complete Myers door hanger line.

Reading Iron Co., 401 N. Broad St., Philadelphia, Pa.

441—Wrought Iron—Information regarding the Genuine Puddled Wrought Iron Products offered by this company.

The Gilbert & Bennett Mfg. Co., Chicago, Ill.

442—Wire Goods—“G & B Wire Goods, Quality Products,” a deluxe handbook of 62 pages featuring sand, gravel and other screens, wire lathing, tree guards, pearl screen cloth, woven wire fences, and other G & B wire goods.

Kewanee Manufacturing Co., Kewanee, Ill.

443—Steel Sash—“Kewanee Building Products,” a 14-page illustrated catalog of Kewanee coal chutes, cellar sash, residence casements, combination sash, fireplace dampers, garbage receivers and other metal specialties.

F. D. Kees Manufacturing Co., Beatrice, Nebr.

444—Hardware Specialties—“Kees Builders Hardware, Catalog No. H-14,” a 28-page illustrated catalog of screen and sash hardware, metal building corners, wall ties, etc.

HOME EQUIPMENT

Frazier Stair Co., Inc., Banksville Ave., Pittsburgh, Pa.

445—Disappearing Stairs—Information regarding the Frazier self balanced disappearing stair offered in five models.

Standard Gas Equipment Corp., 18 E. 41st St., New York City.

446—Kitchen Ranges—“This New Cooking,” a 32-page gas range catalog that will interest housewives because of its recipes, ideas for convenient kitchen arrangement, and details of the Smooth-top gas range which makes possible “one burner meals.”

Lightolier Co., 11 E. 36th St., New York City.

447—Lighting Fixtures—“Lightolier Style Book for 1934-1935,” a big 96-page handbook illustrating the Lightolier line, printed for distribution to those professionally or commercially engaged in the field of lighting equipment.

HEATING AND AIR CONDITIONING

National Radiator Corp., Johnstown, Pa.

448—Concealed Radiation—“Invisible Warmth,” a collection of data sheets, spirally bound, presenting the Aero Convector for concealed radiation.

Universal Insulation Co., 120 S. LaSalle St., Chicago, Ill.

449—Insulation—“Your Fuel Savings Pay for This High Efficiency Insulation,” an informative folder regarding Unifil, together with a sample envelope of this interesting fireproof, expanded mica insulation material.

Ilg Electric Ventilating Co., Chicago, Ill.

450—Air Conditioning—“Ilgair Cooling and Air Conditioning”; 24 pages of photographs of retail stores and other business buildings from coast to coast air conditioned, with instructive details of how the results were accomplished.

Kelvinator Corp., 14250 Plymouth Rd., Detroit, Mich.

451—Air Conditioning—“Kelvinator Exact Selection Air Conditioning,” an illustrated brochure of 20 pages for architects, engineers, contractors, manufacturers, merchants and home owners showing recommended practice in air conditioning.

Fairbanks, Morse & Co., 900 S. Wabash Ave., Chicago, Ill.

452—Stokers—“Fairbanks-Morse Automatic Coal Burners,” 4-page data sheet
